BODY RULE — ABSOLUTE: these are young fighters who walk twenty kilometres a day and eat badly. EVERY MAN IS LEAN AND HARD WITH A FLAT STOMACH — whip-thin, wiry, sinewy, rangy or compactly athletic. Visible collarbones, tendons in the forearms, hollow under the cheekbone, narrow waists, dense flat muscle without bulk. ABSOLUTELY NOBODY IS FAT: no bellies, no paunch, no gut, no soft middle, no double chin, no jowls, no heavy hips, nobody overweight, and equally nobody bodybuilt or gym-inflated. Nobody looks older than thirty — no grey beards, no white beards, no old men, no lined elderly faces, no stooped posture.

FACES — HARD AND HOSTILE, THIS IS THE MOOD OF THE WHOLE SHEET: nobody smiles, nobody is blank or neutral, nobody is friendly. Every man looks straight down the lens with a hard, cold, unwelcoming stare — jaw set, mouth closed and tight, brow low, eyes direct and unblinking, the look of men who have already decided about you. The hostility is DIFFERENT ON EVERY FACE and never a mask: one openly furious with the nostrils flared, one flat and dead-eyed, one coldly contemptuous with the chin lifted, one stony and patient, one seething with the jaw muscle showing, one bored and dangerous, one narrow-eyed and calculating, one hollow and burnt-out, one glaring from under the brow, one grimly amused with no warmth in it, one sullen, one appraising and unimpressed. Real human faces holding a real look, not actors pulling a face — no grimacing, no snarling, no bared teeth, no open mouths, no shouting, no theatrics.

BEARD RULE — ABSOLUTE: EVERY SINGLE MAN HAS A BEARD, without exception, and they are all young men's beards — black or dark brown, none grey, none white. No two are alike: full and long, thick and short, dense and squared off at the bottom, wiry and unkempt, curly, patchy and joined only along the jaw, thin and sparse, a heavy beard with a shaved upper lip, a beard dyed with henna to a dull rust, a soft young beard that has never been cut. Nobody clean-shaven, nobody with stubble only, nobody with a moustache alone.

SCARF RULE — ABSOLUTE, EVERY MAN HAS ONE: every fighter wears a large CHECKED COTTON SCARF — a shemagh / keffiyeh-type cloth with a woven grid or crosshatch check and knotted fringe at the ends — wound round the NECK and shoulders. All of them dusty, faded and low-saturation: dirty black-and-cream check, dust-grey check, faded brown check, washed-out olive check, greyed-out red-and-cream check gone almost pink with sun, a check so faded the pattern barely reads. NO TWO SCARVES SHARE A PATTERN, A COLOUR OR A WAY OF BEING WORN: loose round the neck with both fringed ends down the chest; wound twice tight to the throat; one end thrown back over a shoulder; bunched up under the chin; hanging open like a towel; tucked into the collar of a waistcoat; and exactly ONE man wears it pulled up over the chin and mouth with his eyes and the rest of his face completely clear.

He holds it with BOTH HANDS across the front of his body at waist height, one hand at the handguard and one at the grip, the MUZZLE ANGLED DOWN TOWARD THE FLOOR and clear of everyone. Nobody has it shouldered, nobody aims, nobody points it at the camera or at another figure, no finger inside a trigger guard. No other weapon appears on this sheet. Photorealistic full-length CASTING AND WARDROBE REFERENCE SHEET for a war film, shot in a photographic studio against a seamless DARK GREY backdrop, identical in look, lighting and background to a professional character reference plate: FIFTEEN young Afghan irregular fighters, ALL AGED BETWEEN TWENTY AND THIRTY, standing in ONE SINGLE STRAIGHT ROW, evenly spaced across the frame, never overlapping, ALL FIFTEEN FACING THE CAMERA DEAD-ON, FRONT VIEW ONLY. Every figure is FULL LENGTH — the whole body in frame from the top of the head to the shoes, feet flat on a plain dark grey floor of the same tone as the backdrop, nothing cropped, nobody cut by the frame edge. BODY RULE — ABSOLUTE: these are young fighters who walk twenty kilometres a day and eat badly. EVERY MAN IS LEAN AND HARD WITH A FLAT STOMACH — whip-thin, wiry, sinewy, rangy or compactly athletic. Visible collarbones, tendons in the forearms, hollow under the cheekbone, narrow waists, dense flat muscle without bulk. ABSOLUTELY NOBODY IS FAT: no bellies, no paunch, no gut, no soft middle, no double chin, no jowls, no heavy hips, nobody overweight, and equally nobody bodybuilt or gym-inflated. Nobody looks older than thirty — no grey beards, no white beards, no old men, no lined elderly faces, no stooped posture.

FACES — HARD AND HOSTILE, THIS IS THE MOOD OF THE WHOLE SHEET: nobody smiles, nobody is blank or neutral, nobody is friendly. Every man looks straight down the lens with a hard, cold, unwelcoming stare — jaw set, mouth closed and tight, brow low, eyes direct and unblinking, the look of men who have already decided about you. The hostility is DIFFERENT ON EVERY FACE and never a mask: one openly furious with the nostrils flared, one flat and dead-eyed, one coldly contemptuous with the chin lifted, one stony and patient, one seething with the jaw muscle showing, one bored and dangerous, one narrow-eyed and calculating, one hollow and burnt-out, one glaring from under the brow, one grimly amused with no warmth in it, one sullen, one appraising and unimpressed. Real human faces holding a real look, not actors pulling a face — no grimacing, no snarling, no bared teeth, no open mouths, no shouting, no theatrics.

BEARD RULE — ABSOLUTE: EVERY SINGLE MAN HAS A BEARD, without exception, and they are all young men's beards — black or dark brown, none grey, none white. No two are alike: full and long, thick and short, dense and squared off at the bottom, wiry and unkempt, curly, patchy and joined only along the jaw, thin and sparse, a heavy beard with a shaved upper lip, a beard dyed with henna to a dull rust, a soft young beard that has never been cut. Nobody clean-shaven, nobody with stubble only, nobody with a moustache alone.

SCARF RULE — ABSOLUTE, EVERY MAN HAS ONE: every fighter wears a large CHECKED COTTON SCARF — a shemagh / keffiyeh-type cloth with a woven grid or crosshatch check and knotted fringe at the ends — wound round the NECK and shoulders. All of them DARK, dusty and low-saturation: black-and-charcoal check, black-and-deep-grey check, dark umber-brown check, near-black olive check, dark oxblood-and-black check, a very dark check so dusty the pattern barely reads. No white in any scarf — where a check would normally be white it is dirty dark grey. NO TWO SCARVES SHARE A PATTERN, A COLOUR OR A WAY OF BEING WORN: loose round the neck with both fringed ends down the chest; wound twice tight to the throat; one end thrown back over a shoulder; bunched up under the chin; hanging open like a towel; tucked into the collar of a waistcoat; and exactly ONE man wears it pulled up over the chin and mouth with his eyes and the rest of his face completely clear.

WEAPON RULE — ABSOLUTE, THE SAME WEAPON FOR ALL FIFTEEN: every man holds an AK-74 assault rifle IN HIS HANDS — the AK-74 specifically, with its slotted muzzle brake and curved magazine. He holds it with BOTH HANDS across the front of his body at waist height, one hand at the handguard and one at the grip, the MUZZLE ANGLED DOWN TOWARD THE FLOOR and clear of everyone. Nobody has it shouldered, nobody aims, nobody points it at the camera or at another figure, no finger inside a trigger guard. No other weapon appears on this sheet. THE RIFLES ARE NOT IDENTICAL COPIES: they differ in furniture, magazine and wear — orange-brown laminated wood handguards and stocks, black polymer furniture, plum-coloured polymer magazines, steel magazines, one with two magazines taped together, one with a folding stock, one with a stock repaired with wire and tape, one with a split handguard bound with cord, one with a rusted muzzle brake. Every one dull, scratched, hand-worn, bluing rubbed off the edges, dust in the seams. No optics, no rails, no lasers, no modern accessories, nothing new, nothing black-and-tactical.

DUST PASS — APPLIES TO ALL FIFTEEN: nothing anybody wears is clean or saturated. Every garment is DUSTY, SUN-BLEACHED AND DESATURATED — a fine pale layer of desert dust worked into the weave, heaviest at the hems, knees, cuffs and shoulders, so colours read chalky and greyed-down rather than bright. Clothes worn every day for years and washed in hard water: faded powdery earth tones, dye gone flat, sweat salt at the collars, old stains, mended seams, frayed hems, dust in the beards and on the sandals. DARK VALUE RULE — OVERRIDES EVERY COLOUR NAMED ANYWHERE BELOW: the whole sheet sits in the DARK half of the scale. Every garment, every turban, every scarf, every waistcoat and every blanket is a DEEP, DARK, DUSTY tone — charcoal, near-black, dark slate, deep grey-brown, dark olive gone almost black, deep umber, dark ash, dust-blackened indigo. Wherever a garment is named below as cream, grey, olive, brown or slate, render it as the DARK version of that tone, several stops down — dark dusty cream is a dirty deep sand-brown, dust-grey is charcoal grey, olive is near-black olive, mud brown is deep umber, slate is dark blue-black. Photorealistic full-length CASTING AND WARDROBE REFERENCE SHEET for a war film, shot in a photographic studio against a seamless DARK GREY backdrop, identical in look, lighting and background to a professional character reference plate: FIFTEEN young Afghan irregular fighters, ALL AGED BETWEEN TWENTY AND THIRTY, standing in ONE SINGLE STRAIGHT ROW, evenly spaced across the frame, never overlapping, ALL FIFTEEN FACING THE CAMERA DEAD-ON, FRONT VIEW ONLY. Every figure is FULL LENGTH — the whole body in frame from the top of the head to the shoes, feet flat on a plain dark grey floor of the same tone as the backdrop, nothing cropped, nobody cut by the frame edge. BODY RULE — ABSOLUTE: these are young fighters who walk twenty kilometres a day and eat badly. EVERY MAN IS LEAN AND HARD WITH A FLAT STOMACH — whip-thin, wiry, sinewy, rangy or compactly athletic. Visible collarbones, tendons in the forearms, hollow under the cheekbone, narrow waists, dense flat muscle without bulk. ABSOLUTELY NOBODY IS FAT: no bellies, no paunch, no gut, no soft middle, no double chin, no jowls, no heavy hips, nobody overweight, and equally nobody bodybuilt or gym-inflated. Nobody looks older than thirty — no grey beards, no white beards, no old men, no lined elderly faces, no stooped posture.

FACES — HARD AND HOSTILE, THIS IS THE MOOD OF THE WHOLE SHEET: nobody smiles, nobody is blank or neutral, nobody is friendly. Every man looks straight down the lens with a hard, cold, unwelcoming stare — jaw set, mouth closed and tight, brow low, eyes direct and unblinking, the look of men who have already decided about you. The hostility is DIFFERENT ON EVERY FACE and never a mask: one openly furious with the nostrils flared, one flat and dead-eyed, one coldly contemptuous with the chin lifted, one stony and patient, one seething with the jaw muscle showing, one bored and dangerous, one narrow-eyed and calculating, one hollow and burnt-out, one glaring from under the brow, one grimly amused with no warmth in it, one sullen, one appraising and unimpressed. No two are alike: full and long, thick and short, dense and squared off at the bottom, wiry and unkempt, curly, patchy and joined only along the jaw, thin and sparse, a heavy beard with a shaved upper lip, a beard dyed with henna to a dull rust, a soft young beard that has never been cut. ETHNIC AND REGIONAL FACE TYPE — WRITTEN PLAINLY: these are TALIBAN FIGHTERS. Strong heavy brow ridges with the eyes set deep underneath, hard high cheekbones, long narrow faces, long jaws, thin mouths, aquiline and hooked noses with high bridges, big ears, prominent Adam's apples on the thin ones. Photorealistic full-length CASTING AND WARDROBE REFERENCE SHEET for a war film, shot in a photographic studio against a seamless DARK GREY backdrop, identical in look, lighting and background to a professional character reference plate: FIFTEEN young Afghan irregular fighters, ALL AGED BETWEEN TWENTY AND THIRTY, standing in ONE SINGLE STRAIGHT ROW, evenly spaced across the frame, never overlapping, ALL FIFTEEN FACING THE CAMERA DEAD-ON, FRONT VIEW ONLY. BODY RULE — ABSOLUTE: these are young fighters who walk twenty kilometres a day and eat badly. EVERY MAN IS LEAN AND HARD WITH A FLAT STOMACH — whip-thin, wiry, sinewy, rangy or compactly athletic. Visible collarbones, tendons in the forearms, hollow under the cheekbone, narrow waists, dense flat muscle without bulk. ABSOLUTELY NOBODY IS FAT: no bellies, no paunch, no gut, no soft middle, no double chin, no jowls, no heavy hips, nobody overweight, and equally nobody bodybuilt or gym-inflated. Nobody looks older than thirty — no grey beards, no white beards, no old men, no lined elderly faces, no stooped posture.

FACES — HARD AND HOSTILE, THIS IS THE MOOD OF THE WHOLE SHEET: nobody smiles, nobody is blank or neutral, nobody is friendly. Every man looks straight down the lens with a hard, cold, unwelcoming stare — jaw set, mouth closed and tight, brow low, eyes direct and unblinking, the look of men who have already decided about you. The hostility is DIFFERENT ON EVERY FACE and never a mask: one openly furious with the nostrils flared, one flat and dead-eyed, one coldly contemptuous with the chin lifted, one stony and patient, one seething with the jaw muscle showing, one bored and dangerous, one narrow-eyed and calculating, one hollow and burnt-out, one glaring from under the brow, one grimly amused with no warmth in it, one sullen, one appraising and unimpressed. Real human faces holding a real look, not actors pulling a face — no grimacing, no snarling, no bared teeth, no open mouths, no shouting, no theatrics.

BEARD RULE — ABSOLUTE: EVERY SINGLE MAN HAS A BEARD, without exception, and they are all young men's beards — black or dark brown, none grey, none white. No two are alike: full and long, thick and short, dense and squared off at the bottom, wiry and unkempt, curly, patchy and joined only along the jaw, thin and sparse, a heavy beard with a shaved upper lip, a beard dyed with henna to a dull rust, a soft young beard that has never been cut. Nobody clean-shaven, nobody with stubble only, nobody with a moustache alone.

ETHNIC AND REGIONAL FACE TYPE — WRITTEN PLAINLY: these are TALIBAN FIGHTERS. They are rural southern Afghan PASHTUN men out of Kandahar and Helmand, and the faces have to read as that specific type at a glance, not as generic extras. Strong heavy brow ridges with the eyes set deep underneath, hard high cheekbones, long narrow faces, long jaws, thin mouths, aquiline and hooked noses with high bridges, big ears, prominent Adam's apples on the thin ones. Skin ruined by wind, altitude and sun — weathered, dry, coarse-pored, sun lines fanning from the outer corner of the eye even on the twenty-year-olds, cracked lips, dust in the creases. Hair and beards black or very dark brown, eyebrows thick, straight and dark, often nearly meeting. Eyes mostly dark brown, but two or three men have the pale grey-green or light hazel eyes that genuinely occur among Pashtuns, and on those faces it reads colder. SEVERAL OF THEM WEAR SURMA: a thin smudged line of black kohl along the upper and lower lash line, an ordinary practice among Pashtun men and a signature look on Taliban fighters — it makes the eyes read harder, blacker and more direct, and it should be clearly visible on four or five of the fifteen and absent on the rest. NOT Arab faces, NOT urban Persian or Iranian faces, NOT Turkish, NOT Indian, NOT Central Asian or Turkic or Hazara faces with epicanthic folds and flat features, NOT smooth modern city faces, NOT western actors in beards — southern Pashtun village men.

SCARF RULE — NOT EVERYONE, AND THAT IS THE POINT: only SOME of them wear a large CHECKED COTTON SCARF — a shemagh / keffiyeh-type cloth with a woven grid or crosshatch check and knotted fringe at the ends — wound round the NECK and shoulders. All of them DARK, dusty and low-saturation: black-and-charcoal check, black-and-deep-grey check, dark umber-brown check, near-black olive check, dark oxblood-and-black check, a very dark check so dusty the pattern barely reads. No white in any scarf — where a check would normally be white it is dirty dark grey. NO TWO SCARVES SHARE A PATTERN, A COLOUR OR A WAY OF BEING WORN: loose round the neck with both fringed ends down the chest; wound twice tight to the throat; one end thrown back over a shoulder; bunched up under the chin; hanging open like a towel; tucked into the collar of a waistcoat; and exactly ONE man wears it pulled up over the chin and mouth with his eyes and the rest of his face completely clear.

Photorealistic full-length CASTING AND WARDROBE REFERENCE SHEET for a war film, shot in a photographic studio against a seamless DARK GREY backdrop, identical in look, lighting and background to a professional character reference plate: FIFTEEN young Afghan irregular fighters, ALL AGED BETWEEN TWENTY AND THIRTY, standing in ONE SINGLE STRAIGHT ROW, evenly spaced across the frame, never overlapping, ALL FIFTEEN FACING THE CAMERA DEAD-ON, FRONT VIEW ONLY. Every figure is FULL LENGTH — the whole body in frame from the top of the head to the shoes, feet flat on a plain dark grey floor of the same tone as the backdrop, nothing cropped, nobody cut by the frame edge. Soft even studio light from the front, gentle falloff, no hard shadows on the backdrop, no rim light, no coloured light, all fifteen lit exactly the same and rendered at exactly the same scale and the same true human proportion.

BODY RULE — ABSOLUTE: these are young fighters who walk twenty kilometres a day and eat badly. EVERY MAN IS LEAN AND HARD WITH A FLAT STOMACH — whip-thin, wiry, sinewy, rangy or compactly athletic. Visible collarbones, tendons in the forearms, hollow under the cheekbone, narrow waists, dense flat muscle without bulk. ABSOLUTELY NOBODY IS FAT: no bellies, no paunch, no gut, no soft middle, no double chin, no jowls, no heavy hips, nobody overweight, and equally nobody bodybuilt or gym-inflated. Nobody looks older than thirty — no grey beards, no white beards, no old men, no lined elderly faces, no stooped posture.

FACES — HARD AND HOSTILE, THIS IS THE MOOD OF THE WHOLE SHEET: nobody smiles, nobody is blank or neutral, nobody is friendly. Every man looks straight down the lens with a hard, cold, unwelcoming stare — jaw set, mouth closed and tight, brow low, eyes direct and unblinking, the look of men who have already decided about you. The hostility is DIFFERENT ON EVERY FACE and never a mask: one openly furious with the nostrils flared, one flat and dead-eyed, one coldly contemptuous with the chin lifted, one stony and patient, one seething with the jaw muscle showing, one bored and dangerous, one narrow-eyed and calculating, one hollow and burnt-out, one glaring from under the brow, one grimly amused with no warmth in it, one sullen, one appraising and unimpressed. Real human faces holding a real look, not actors pulling a face — no grimacing, no snarling, no bared teeth, no open mouths, no shouting, no theatrics.

BEARD RULE — ABSOLUTE: EVERY SINGLE MAN HAS A BEARD, without exception, and they are all young men's beards — black or dark brown, none grey, none white. No two are alike: full and long, thick and short, dense and squared off at the bottom, wiry and unkempt, curly, patchy and joined only along the jaw, thin and sparse, a heavy beard with a shaved upper lip, a beard dyed with henna to a dull rust, a soft young beard that has never been cut. Nobody clean-shaven, nobody with stubble only, nobody with a moustache alone.

ETHNIC AND REGIONAL FACE TYPE — WRITTEN PLAINLY: these are TALIBAN FIGHTERS. They are rural southern Afghan PASHTUN men out of Kandahar and Helmand, and the faces have to read as that specific type at a glance, not as generic extras. Strong heavy brow ridges with the eyes set deep underneath, hard high cheekbones, long narrow faces, long jaws, thin mouths, aquiline and hooked noses with high bridges, big ears, prominent Adam's apples on the thin ones. Skin ruined by wind, altitude and sun — weathered, dry, coarse-pored, sun lines fanning from the outer corner of the eye even on the twenty-year-olds, cracked lips, dust in the creases. Hair and beards black or very dark brown, eyebrows thick, straight and dark, often nearly meeting. Eyes mostly dark brown, but two or three men have the pale grey-green or light hazel eyes that genuinely occur among Pashtuns, and on those faces it reads colder. SEVERAL OF THEM WEAR SURMA: a thin smudged line of black kohl along the upper and lower lash line, an ordinary practice among Pashtun men and a signature look on Taliban fighters — it makes the eyes read harder, blacker and more direct, and it should be clearly visible on four or five of the fifteen and absent on the rest. NOT Arab faces, NOT urban Persian or Iranian faces, NOT Turkish, NOT Indian, NOT Central Asian or Turkic or Hazara faces with epicanthic folds and flat features, NOT smooth modern city faces, NOT western actors in beards — southern Pashtun village men.

SCARF RULE — NOT EVERYONE, AND THAT IS THE POINT: only SOME of them wear a large CHECKED COTTON SCARF — a shemagh / keffiyeh-type cloth with a woven grid or crosshatch check and knotted fringe at the ends — wound round the NECK and shoulders. All of them DARK, dusty and low-saturation: black-and-charcoal check, black-and-deep-grey check, dark umber-brown check, near-black olive check, dark oxblood-and-black check, a very dark check so dusty the pattern barely reads. No white in any scarf — where a check would normally be white it is dirty dark grey. NO TWO SCARVES SHARE A PATTERN, A COLOUR OR A WAY OF BEING WORN: loose round the neck with both fringed ends down the chest; wound twice tight to the throat; one end thrown back over a shoulder; bunched up under the chin; hanging open like a towel; tucked into the collar of a waistcoat; and exactly ONE man wears it pulled up over the chin and mouth with his eyes and the rest of his face completely clear.
WHO GETS A SCARF AND WHO DOES NOT — THIS OVERRIDES THE SCARF NAMED IN ANY ROSTER LINE BELOW: only men 2, 5, 9, 11 and 14 wear the CHECKED scarf. Men 4, 8 and 13 wear instead a PLAIN DARK CLOTH — no check, no pattern — wound loosely round the neck, one of them a strip torn off a blanket. Men 1, 3, 6, 7, 10, 12 and 15 wear NOTHING ON THE NECK AT ALL: bare open collar, throat and collarbones showing, dust on the skin. Nobody outside the five named men has a checked scarf anywhere on his body.

WEAPON RULE — ABSOLUTE, THE SAME WEAPON FOR ALL FIFTEEN: every man holds an AK-74 assault rifle IN HIS HANDS — the AK-74 specifically, with its slotted muzzle brake and curved magazine. He holds it with BOTH HANDS across the front of his body at waist height, one hand at the handguard and one at the grip, the MUZZLE ANGLED DOWN TOWARD THE FLOOR and clear of everyone. Nobody has it shouldered, nobody aims, nobody points it at the camera or at another figure, no finger inside a trigger guard. No other weapon appears on this sheet. THE RIFLES ARE NOT IDENTICAL COPIES: they differ in furniture, magazine and wear — orange-brown laminated wood handguards and stocks, black polymer furniture, plum-coloured polymer magazines, steel magazines, one with two magazines taped together, one with a folding stock, one with a stock repaired with wire and tape, one with a split handguard bound with cord, one with a rusted muzzle brake. Every one dull, scratched, hand-worn, bluing rubbed off the edges, dust in the seams. No optics, no rails, no lasers, no modern accessories, nothing new, nothing black-and-tactical.

DUST PASS — APPLIES TO ALL FIFTEEN: nothing anybody wears is clean or saturated. Every garment is DUSTY, SUN-BLEACHED AND DESATURATED — a fine pale layer of desert dust worked into the weave, heaviest at the hems, knees, cuffs and shoulders, so colours read chalky and greyed-down rather than bright. Clothes worn every day for years and washed in hard water: faded powdery earth tones, dye gone flat, sweat salt at the collars, old stains, mended seams, frayed hems, dust in the beards and on the sandals. DARK VALUE RULE — OVERRIDES EVERY COLOUR NAMED ANYWHERE BELOW: the whole sheet sits in the DARK half of the scale. Every garment, every turban, every scarf, every waistcoat and every blanket is a DEEP, DARK, DUSTY tone — charcoal, near-black, dark slate, deep grey-brown, dark olive gone almost black, deep umber, dark ash, dust-blackened indigo. The dust on them reads as a pale grey film ON TOP of a dark cloth, never as a pale cloth. Wherever a garment is named below as cream, grey, olive, brown or slate, render it as the DARK version of that tone, several stops down — dark dusty cream is a dirty deep sand-brown, dust-grey is charcoal grey, olive is near-black olive, mud brown is deep umber, slate is dark blue-black. NOTHING PALE, NOTHING LIGHT, NOTHING WHITE, no bright fabric, nothing lighter than a mid-dark tone anywhere on the sheet; the lightest thing in the frame is the dust film and the men's skin. Overall the row reads DARK against the dark grey backdrop, held apart from it only by the dust, the texture and the front light.

WARDROBE WORLD: long shalwar kameez in charcoal, near-black, dark slate blue-black, deep umber brown, dark olive gone almost black, dirty deep sand-brown, hanging loose on lean bodies; thin dark wool waistcoats; a rough patu wool blanket over one shoulder; heads varied — black, white or dust-brown turbans wound differently on every man, embroidered skullcaps, one flat woollen pakol cap only, several men bare-headed; footwear varied — cracked leather sandals, plastic sandals, cheap trainers, scuffed boots, one man in odd mismatched shoes. GEAR AND LOAD-BEARING — THIS IS THE SECOND MOST IMPORTANT THING ON THE SHEET AFTER THE FACES, AND IT MUST BE VISIBLY DIFFERENT MAN TO MAN. Everybody carries spare magazines and everybody carries them differently, all of it home-assembled, canvas and leather, all of it DARK and dust-worn. The types available, all period-correct and none of them western-issue:
— A CANVAS AK CHEST RIG worn over the shalwar kameez: a dark olive or charcoal canvas vest-front with three large square magazine pockets across the chest, two smaller grenade pockets, buckled canvas straps over the shoulders and round the waist, flaps closed with a strip of webbing and a tab, the canvas gone soft and pale at the fold lines.
— A HEAVIER FOUR-POCKET CANVAS CHEST RIG of the same family, taller on the chest, one flap missing, replaced with a strip of cloth.
— A DARK WOOL WAISTCOAT USED AS THE RIG ITSELF: an ordinary sleeveless waistcoat with curved magazines shoved straight into the inside chest pockets so the shape of them prints through the cloth, one magazine sticking out at the top, pockets sagging and stretched out of shape.
— A LEATHER BANDOLIER over one shoulder and across the chest, hand-stitched, with loops and small closed pouches, the leather cracked and grey with dust.
— A LEATHER BELT AROUND THE WAIST with two or three canvas pouches on it, plus a knife in a leather sheath.
— A CLOTH SHOULDER BAG on a long strap hanging at the hip with the corners of magazines showing through the fabric.
— A LENGTH OF CLOTH WOUND ROUND THE WAIST as a sash with a spare magazine pushed into it and nothing else.
HOW IT IS SPREAD ACROSS THIS ROW — assign exactly like this, and note it is a DIFFERENT spread from the other sheet: men 2, 6 and 13 wear the three-pocket canvas chest rig, each a different dark colour and a different state of wear; men 4 and 11 wear the heavier four-pocket rig; men 1, 9 and 12 use the dark wool waistcoat as the rig with magazines printing through the pockets; men 5, 7 and 14 wear the leather bandolier across the chest; men 3 and 15 have only the belt with canvas pouches; man 8 has the cloth shoulder bag; man 10 has just the cloth sash at the waist with one magazine in it. Extras scattered so no two men are kitted the same: a dented water bottle on a strap on one man, a small canvas satchel on another, a cheap plastic wristwatch, a coil of rope, a folded blanket strap.
NOTHING WESTERN OR MILITARY-ISSUE: no plate carriers, no modern nylon or MOLLE webbing, no plastic buckles, no camouflage uniforms, no helmets, no ballistic goggles, no night-vision, no radios with antennas, no pouches with velcro, no branded tactical gear — everything is canvas, leather, cloth, metal buckles and hand stitching.

THE VIEWPOINT — IDENTICAL TO THE INTACT PLATE: camera on the flat roof of the corner house, standing BEHIND ITS CONCRETE PARAPET, which runs across the bottom third of the frame as a pale horizontal band with its capping slab and a few spent brass cases lying on it. Long-ish lens, flat perspective, ANAMORPHIC 2.39:1, horizon roughly level, no drone move — a static plate.

WHAT MUST STAY THE SAME AS THE INTACT PLATE, BUILDING FOR BUILDING: the same dense low-rise Kabul block of two- and three-storey flat-roofed houses in bare tan concrete block and sand-coloured render; the same rooflines stepping away on both sides with BLACK PLASTIC WATER TANKS and grey SATELLITE DISHES on them; the same line of leaning CONCRETE POWER POLES down both sides with slack cables sagging between them; the same unpaved dust-and-gravel street with no kerbs; the same BURNT-OUT AND STRIPPED CARS parked along both sides and abandoned at angles in the middle — saloons and one estate, paint gone, glass gone, tyres flat or missing; the same barred windows, roller shutters, low courtyard walls and doorways. Same time of day, same hard high sun, same warm honey-and-sand palette, same heat haze at the far end.

WHAT IS NEW — THE DAMAGE, PARTIAL AND UNEVEN, NOT TOTAL FLATTENING: the block has been hit in patches, so ruined and untouched stand side by side.
— TWO OR THREE FACADES HAVE COME DOWN: on the left, mid-street, the whole front wall of a two-storey house has DELAMINATED and collapsed outward into the road as a fan of block and render, leaving the rooms behind it open to the air like a doll's house — bare walls, a hanging light flex, a door standing in a wall that no longer has a wall beside it.
— ONE ROOF SLAB HAS DROPPED at one corner, tipped down into the storey below with bent REBAR standing up out of the broken edge.
— A COURTYARD WALL further up has burst outward across the pavement in a low spill of rubble.
— RUBBLE TONGUES spill out of every damaged building and narrow the street to a single winding path.

High aerial drone photograph looking down at an Afghan city in a dry river valley, shot from about a hundred and fifty metres up at a steep downward angle of roughly sixty degrees — high enough to read the whole layout of the village and the land around it, close enough that individual walls, roofs and paths are clear, and not a flat straight-down map view.

Narrow dirt alleys wind between the walls with no straight lines anywhere. One unpaved road comes in from the distance in a long curve, tyre tracks and dust on it, a single battered pickup parked at the edge of the village and a hand cart tipped on its side.
